items.prompt: rain that fell on the hills is lying in (31) ........ under the surface
items.evidence: rain that fell on high ground sits in gravel below the surface
items.explanation: At the point where the high ground meets the plain, rain that fell higher up collects in gravel below the surface.

items.prompt: dig a tunnel back towards the well, rising at roughly one in a (32) ........
items.evidence: the figure is worth remembering: about one in a thousand
items.explanation: A gradient of one in a hundred is the figure for the air shafts, not the tunnel; the channel itself should rise at roughly one in a thousand.

items.prompt: they take out the spoil, bring in air and, above all, allow (33) ........
items.evidence: they give access for maintenance for as long as the system is in use
items.explanation: The vertical shafts have three functions; according to the speaker, the most important is that they give access for maintenance for as long as the system is in use.

items.prompt: under (34) ........ per cent of it is lost on the way
items.evidence: Losses from an underground channel are under five per cent
items.explanation: Losses from an open channel are around a third, while an underground channel keeps losses under five per cent.

items.evidence: almost every system of this type ends in a holding pond
items.explanation: The flow cannot be switched off, so the water runs day and night; that's why almost every system of this type ends in a holding pond.
